questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests the ability to design end-to-end provenance systems with multi-region operational requirements, tenant isolation, and production-grade constraints.

## Key Concepts
- CNF provenance using Cosign and SPDX SBOMs
- Per-tenant KMS key management and rotation
- Attestation storage in SigStore with Rekor transparency
- Admission control via ImagePolicyWebhook and Kyverno
- Revocation through CRLs and transparency logs
- Offline edge verification with bundled certificates
- Minimal scheduling impact through async verification

## Code Example
```yaml
# Example Kyverno policy for CNF provenance enforcement
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: cnf-provenance-policy
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: verify-image-signature
    match:
      any:
      - resources:
          kinds:
          - Pod
    verifyImages:
    - imageReferences:
      - "*"
      required: true
      attestors:
      - entries:
        - keys:
            kms: "aws-kms://key-id"
      attestations:
      - predicateType: "spdx"
        conditions:
        - all:
          - key: "{{ attestor.metadata.name }}"
            operator: Equals
            value: "tenant-{{ request.namespace }}"
```

## Why This Is Asked

Tests practical knowledge of per-tenant guardrails in CNF platforms, focusing on image provenance, SBOM validation, and namespace annotations to surface compliance.

## Key Concepts

- Kubernetes admission webhooks and ConfigMap-driven policies
- Cosign signatures tied to tenant keys (KMS-backed)
- SPDX SBOM presence and component checks
- Namespace annotations as compliance badges

## Code Example

```yaml
# Policy ConfigMap (cnf-policies namespace)
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cnf-policy
  namespace: cnf-policies
data:
  policy.json: |
    {
      "tenants": {
        "tenant-a": {
          "requiresSignature": true,
          "requiredSBOMComponent": "openssl"
        }
      }
    }
```

```yaml
# Test manifest (namespace: tenant-a)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-cnf
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: tenant-a-cnf
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: registry.example.com/cnf/gateway:1.0.0
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
```

- How would you handle key rotation for tenant KMS keys within this policy?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design a compliant telemetry stack for CNF gateways with multi-tenant segregation and data privacy.

## Key Concepts
- Telemetry pipelines (OpenTelemetry, Fluent Bit) across logs and traces
- Tenant context propagation and isolation
- PII masking via in-line filters (e.g., Lua) before forwarding
- Loki/Jaeger exporters and per-tenant pipelines

## Code Example
```yaml
# Fluent Bit ConfigMap snippet (Lua filter used for masking)
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: fluent-bit-pp
data:
  lua-filter.lua: |
    function filter(tag, dt)
      if dt["message"] ~= nil then
        dt["message"] = (dt["message"]):gsub("%w+@%w+%.%w+", "[REDACTED_EMAIL]")
      end
      return dt
    end
```
```yaml
# OTEL collector snippet (simplified)
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: otel-collector-config
data:
  collector.yaml: |-
    receivers:
      otlp:
        protocols:
          grpc: {}
          http: {}
    processors:
      attributes:
        actions: [insert]
        keys: [tenant_id]
        from_context: true
    exporters:
      jaeger: {}
      loki: {}
    service:
      pipelines:
        traces:
          receivers: [otlp]
          processors: [attributes]
          exporters: [jaeger]
        logs:
          receivers: [otlp]
          processors: [attributes]
          exporters: [loki]
```

- What metrics would verify isolation and masking effectiveness?

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cnf.api.spec
data:
  tenant-a.yaml: |-
    openapi: 3.0.0
    paths:
      /api/resource:
        post:
          requestBody:
            required: true
            content:
              application/json:
                schema:
                  type: object
                  required: [name]
                  properties:
                    name:
                      type: string
          responses:
            '200':
              description: Success
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: api-gateway
spec:
  selector:
    app: gateway
  ports:
    - port: 8080
      targetPort: 8080
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: api-gateway
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gateway
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: gateway
          image: nginx:1.21
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          volumeMounts:
            - name: spec-config
              mountPath: /etc/cnf-specs
              readOnly: true
        - name: validator-sidecar
          image: validator:latest
          env:
            - name: SPEC_PATH
              value: /etc/cnf-specs
          volumeMounts:
            - name: spec-config
              mountPath: /etc/cnf-specs
              readOnly: true
      volumes:
        - name: spec-config
          configMap:
            name: cnf.api.spec
```

## Why This Is Asked
Assesses multi-region, multi-tenant certificate rotation with in-cluster CA, CSR flow, and DR planning.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes CRD design for TenantCertificateRotation
- In-cluster CA issuance and CSR approval workflow
- Short-lived certs and seamless rotation without downtime
- Disaster recovery and observability of rotation latency

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Certificate
metadata:
  name: tenant-cert
spec:
  secretName: tenant-tls
  duration: 24h
  dnsNames:
  - gateway.example.com
  # ...
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you verify rotation correctness under peak load?
- What are failure modes and how would you detect them in metrics?
